clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock opened the week at 7:43 p.m. and closed at the same time, a movement of only six one-hundredths of a minute. This near-stillness reflects a week of intense, opposing pressures—aggressive federal enforcement pulling one way, judicial and civic resistance pulling the other—that largely canceled each other out.

grand_total_points.note: The net clock movement was just one-tenth of a minute, the smallest possible signal given the volume of underlying activity.

delta_summary.moral_floor: The moral floor continued to erode this week, with executive rhetoric and enforcement actions prioritizing political control over public duty, while judicial and state-level resistance provided partial but insufficient counterweight.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: The week's near-zero clock movement should not be read as calm. It reflects ferocious activity pulling in opposite directions—aggressive federal enforcement and information control on one side, judicial intervention, congressional oversight, and civic mobilization on the other—leaving the structural measure nearly unchanged even as democratic strain intensified.

long_synopsis: Federal agents detained a five-year-old boy and his father, then swept up two more children from his school days later. These acts were part of a broader Minneapolis campaign of raids reaching churches, businesses, and immigrant neighborhoods. The killing of Alex Pretti by federal agents became a second flashpoint, drawing bipartisan calls for investigation, a state agency's own rebuttal website, and a presidential dispatch of his border czar. Courts intervened repeatedly, ordering releases and preserving evidence, while Congress used funding leverage over Homeland Security. Meanwhile, the EPA rescinded its climate finding and suspended dissenting staff, and election administration in Minnesota and Georgia absorbed new federal pressure. The Democracy Clock barely moved, reflecting intense, canceling pressures from multiple directions rather than a single decisive shift.
short_synopsis: Minneapolis became the center of a week defined by child detentions, a fatal shooting by federal agents, and fierce institutional pushback. Courts, Congress, and citizens pressed back hard against expanding federal power, holding the needle nearly still even as intensity surged on every front.
